Rajendra Kumar Walia vs State Of U.P. And Another on 18
December, 2023

Author: Renu Agarwal
Bench: Renu Agarwal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:239338
Court No. - 77
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 53105 of 2023
Applicant :- Rajendra Kumar Walia
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mrs. Renu Agarwal,J. 
1. Supplementary affidavit filed today in the Court, which is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri S. I. Jafari, learned Senior Advocate, assisted by Sri Shrish Chandra, learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State-respondent and perused the material brought on record on the instant application for bail.
3.
The present application under Section 439 Cr.P.C has been filed seeking bail in Case Crime No.558 of 2023, under Sections 420, 409, 120-B of IPC, Police Station Kanker Kheda, District Meerut.
4. Learned counsel for the accused-applicant submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the instant case as he is father of main culprit/ co-accused Vineet Walia.

According to Rajendra Kumar Walia vs State Of U.P. And Another on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176441039/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the version of FIR entire transaction was done by co-accused Vineet Walia and all the jewelries entrusted by the informant to him.
Main allegations is against co-accused Vineet Walia and no specific allegation is made against the present applicant.
Applicant has no prior criminal history apart form present case.
The transaction is of civil nature that too is against the co-accused Vineet Walia.
Applicant is old person aged about 75 yeas and is not beneficiary of the transactions in question.
There is no apprehension of the applicant fleeing away from the judicial custody or tempering with the prosecution witnesses.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 12.10.2023 and in case he is granted bail, he will not misuse the liberty and would cooperate in the trial proceedings.
4. On the other hand, learned AGA has opposed the prayer for bail but could not controvert the aforesaid facts.

5. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and taking into account that this is civil dispute and all the allegations are made against the co-accused Vineet Walia, who is son of the applicant, no specific allegation is made against the present applicant, applicant is old person aged about 75 yeas and is not beneficiary of the transactions in question, there is no apprehension of the applicant fleeing away from the judicial custody or tempering with the prosecution witnesses,
applicant has no relationship in any way with the informant, case of present applicant is squarely covered with the case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in 2021 (10) SCC 773 and Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigaton and others Manu/SC/0851/2022, applicant is languishing in jail since 12.10.2023 and undertakes that in case he is granted bail, he will not misuse the liberty and would cooperate in the trial proceedings,
without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, it would be appropriate to enlarge the accused-applicants on bail.

sentences.text:
6. Let applicant Rajendra Kumar Walia be released on bail in the above case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of Court concerned with the following conditions :-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

(v) The applicant shall also furnish an undertaking from the sureties that the properties (movable/immovable) which are the basis of accepting the surety, shall not be disposed of by them till the conclusion of trial.
(vi) The applicant shall also give an undertaking to the effect that he will not change his address without prior intimation to the trial court concerned.
